A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a diagnostic toolkit for understanding how data support the use of a GP as the distribution of random effects in a mixed model and for understanding how adding covariates moves variation out of the GP part of the fit.
we provide a diagnostic toolkit for understanding the data's support of the random‐effect distribution in linear models.

we provide a set of tools to understand the fit of mixed‐effects models with GPs as random effects, including tools to understand how the fit of a covariate moves variation out of the GP part of the fit and tools to understand the effect of smoothing the data before fitting the GP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GP distribution of random effects can be understood in terms of a spectral decomposition and that the AVP can be adapted to the GP setting.
the GP is a useful distribution of random effects, but that the spectral approximation is useful in understanding the GP and its role in mixed‐model fitting.
, for linear‐mixed‐model analysis of data observed on a grid, it is often possible to use the tools and intuition of linear regression to understand the fit.
